sources.entry: Saltcorn - No-code database application builder for web and mobile applications. One platform for user interface, data backend, durable workflows, email, PDF generation, and AI applications. (Source Code) MIT Docker/Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Saltcorn is an open source no-code database application builder for creating web and mobile database apps, self-hosted via Node.js with PostgreSQL or SQLite.
summary.what_it_does: Saltcorn lets you build web and mobile database applications using views, datatypes, layouts and actions without writing code. The repository holds the core codebase, which can be used to self-host a single instance or run a multitenant instance. It can be installed from npm as a CLI (@saltcorn/cli) or run via Docker. The README describes PostgreSQL as the main database backend, with SQLite selectable through an SQLITE_FILEPATH setting for desktop trials. It includes a CLI with commands for serving the app, installing plugins, running tests and developing local plugins. Mobile app builds are supported, though their dependencies are excluded from the standard Docker image.
use_cases: build a custom database web app without coding
create a mobile app backed by a database
run a multitenant app hosting service
prototype a data app on a desktop
notable: Multitenant mode can host many apps under subdomains on one instance
Plugin system with local plugin development and dev server with auto-rebuild
Built-in durable workflows, email, PDF generation and AI application support
Automated Linux server installer (saltcorn-install / saltcorn setup)
caveats: Mobile app builds need large extra dependencies, so they are excluded from the standard Docker image
multi_node mode only works with PostgreSQL and needs a shared drive across nodes
The README says a 1GB VM can have upgrade issues; 2GB is recommended
